problem_type: release promotion blocked by the developer pre-push receipt hook
symptom: Desktop Release run 36325671938 for v0.22.2 failed at 'Create immutable tag': git push origin v0.22.2 was rejected by '[ponytail-receipt] BLOCKED: 没有可读的分支评审收据'. Nothing was published; the release only went through after the tag was created on a developer machine and the workflow was re-run.
direct_cause: The promote job runs pnpm install, whose postinstall installs the repository pre-push hook into the runner. verifyPushReceipt then demanded a Ponytail receipt for the tag ref, and the runner never has one.
class_root: verifyPushReceipt treated every non-deletion ref as new content needing review. It had no notion that a ref pointing at a commit already contained in a remote-tracking branch pushes no new content, so any push of already-published history (release tags on merged commits, re-pushing a reviewed commit under another name) was blocked wherever no receipt existed.
affected_population: Every Desktop Release promotion (CI runner, no receipt) when the tag does not already exist
Developers pushing a tag or branch that points at commits already on origin
entry_points: .github/workflows/desktop-release.yml 'Create immutable tag' step (git push origin $RELEASE_TAG) via the installed hook

invariant_owner_layer.why: verifyPushReceipt is the single place that decides which pushed refs need a receipt; the hook adapter only forwards Git's ref list.

external_sources.purpose: Confirm pre-push receives <local ref> <local object name> <remote ref> <remote object name> lines, where the local object for an annotated tag is the tag object.
Confirm for-each-ref --contains lists refs whose history contains the given commit, peeling a tag object to its commit.

invariants: A pushed ref needs a review receipt only if its object is not already contained in some remote-tracking branch; the exemption depends on whether the content is already on the remote, never on whether the ref is a tag.
Refs that do carry new content are still checked against the receipt tree and merge-base exactly as before, including in mixed pushes.

door_reduction.why_not: node scripts/door-map.mjs verifyPushReceipt alreadyOnRemote --roots=scripts: the hook adapter is the only caller of verifyPushReceipt, and alreadyOnRemote is the new predicate inside the same owner. No second decision point exists.

generality_proof: The rule applies to every ref kind and every caller of the hook (CI runner, developer machine) because it asks Git whether the object is already in remote-tracking history rather than special-casing release tags, CI environment variables, or workflow names.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Decide which pushes carry new content: only commits no remote-tracking branch knows about need the gates stamp (the receipt gate that used to decide this was deleted on 2026-10-02).

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Forwards Git's ref list to verifyPushReceipt and prints the exemption reason; no logic of its own.
The job never runs pnpm install, so no repository hook is installed on that runner.

recurrence.reason: Every release promotion hits this path whenever the tag is new; it silently relied on the tag having been created by hand (the 0.22.1 run succeeded because the tag already existed).
same_class_scan: Grep of .github/workflows for git push and pnpm install: only desktop-release.yml both installs dependencies and pushes; download-stats.yml pushes without installing.
node scripts/door-map.mjs verifyPushReceipt alreadyOnRemote --roots=scripts returned the two doors above.

prevention.invariant: Only refs whose content is not yet on the remote require a receipt.
prevention.failure_mode: If the exemption is removed, the node-test that pushes an annotated tag on a remote-contained commit without a receipt fails; if the exemption keys on ref type instead of content, the test that pushes a tag on a new commit fails.
prevention.strategy: Ask Git (for-each-ref --contains over refs/remotes) per ref before loading the receipt; stale remote-tracking refs can only reduce exemptions.

legacy_paths.rationale: The existing verifier is corrected in place; no workflow bypass (--no-verify, core.hooksPath) is added.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Uses git for-each-ref only; no dependency changes.

migration: None. Existing receipts and the release workflow are unchanged; the next promotion creates the tag without manual steps.
residual_risks: If the runner's checkout has no remote-tracking refs (for example a shallow single-ref fetch), the exemption does not apply and the tag push is blocked again; desktop-release.yml currently fetches all branches.
